options.A: Systemic toxicity from drug absorption
options.B: Re-expansion pulmonary edema
options.C: Severe local pleuritic chest pain
options.D: Permanent loss of the patient's voice box

explanation: You nailed it! Intrapleural treatments deal with the chest cavity and lungs, not the larynx or vocal cords, so voice loss has nothing to do with this procedure.

question: Which type of teeth are primarily designed for biting and cutting food?

options.A: Incisors
options.B: Canines
options.C: Premolars
options.D: Molars

explanation: Incisors are the sharp, flat front teeth used specifically for biting off pieces of food. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do tightly coiled hair textures often tend to feel drier than straight hair?

options.A: The scalp produces significantly less sebum in these individuals
options.B: Frequent washing strips away the natural protective proteins
options.C: Curly hair follicles lack sebaceous glands entirely
options.D: Natural scalp oils have trouble traveling down the curved hair shaft

explanation: Because of the bends and turns in coils and curls, the natural oils from the scalp have a harder time sliding down the full length of the hair. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is good nutrition and protein especially vital for patients healing from deep wounds like pressure sores?

options.A: Cells need building blocks to repair the extracellular matrix and regenerate tissue
options.B: Nutrition stops nervous tissue from sending pain signals to the brain
options.C: Vitamins automatically clean bacteria out of closed body cavities
options.D: Proteins completely replace the need for blood circulation in wounds

explanation: Your body can't rebuild damaged tissue out of nothing! Good protein gives cells the raw materials they need to patch things up.

question: Why does nursing leadership need to carry out regular program evaluations?

options.A: It reveals if the interventions are actually improving health outcomes
options.B: It ensures that no patient ever complains about the hospital
options.C: It proves that administrative staff are smarter than clinical nurses
options.D: It gives staff a reason to stop working for several months

explanation: Spot on! Evaluation tells us whether our hard work and resources actually solved the health problem we targeted.

question: Why is educating family caregivers considered a critical step before sending a patient on leave?

options.A: It ensures the family can diagnose new psychiatric disorders
options.B: It legally transfers all medical liability from the doctor to the family
options.C: It helps caregivers recognize early warning signs of relapse and manage stress safely
options.D: It prevents the family from ever asking questions

explanation: An informed family is a strong support system! Educating them helps catch tiny behavioral changes before they turn into a full crisis.

question: Why do we often describe the pelvic floor as a hammock?

options.A: It swings freely between the hips to cushion the baby's head
options.B: It stretches from the pubic bone to the coccyx to support pelvic organs
options.C: It hangs loosely from the abdominal wall to protect the intestines
options.D: It attaches only to the hip joints to assist with walking

explanation: Great thinking! Just like a hammock, these muscles stretch right from front to back to cradle the bladder, uterus, and bowels.

question: What should you do if you notice a clinical policy on your ward is outdated or confusing?

options.A: Change the national health laws to match personal preference
options.B: Report the gap through official institutional channels
options.C: Throw away all printed copies of the hospital rulebook
options.D: Keep the information secret from all other staff members

explanation: Using official reporting channels helps management fix and update policies safely without encouraging risky shortcuts on the ward.

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for developing osteoarthritis?

options.A: Regular aerobic exercise
options.B: High dietary sugar
options.C: Advanced age
options.D: Cold weather climates

explanation: That is correct! As we grow older, our joints experience years of natural use, making age the number one risk factor for joint wear and tear.

question: Which of these is a common everyday distraction during a home health visit?

options.A: Frequent interruptions from attending physicians
options.B: Mandatory shift-change meetings in the hallway
options.C: Strict hospital visiting hour regulations
options.D: Background noise from household sources and family members

explanation: Unlike quiet hospital wards, homes are full of life! TVs playing, pets barking, and family chatting can make focusing a bit tricky.

question: How do touchless gesture controls help nurses working in sterile environments like the operating room?

options.A: They eliminate the need for patient identification wristbands
options.B: They make computer screens brighter in dark surgical suites
options.C: They allow computers to run without needing any electricity
options.D: They let nurses interact with software without breaking sterile technique

explanation: Brilliant! Gesture controls let you check screens and records with a wave of your hand, keeping your sterile gloves clean and safe.

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving out medications in a day hospital?

options.A: Monitoring clients for side effects like extrapyramidal symptoms
options.B: Hiding the medication from family members
options.C: Prescribing higher dosages when symptoms worsen
options.D: Allowing clients to choose whatever drug they prefer

explanation: Correct! Since clients spend a lot of time outside the hospital, nurses must watch closely for any unwanted drug reactions.

question: A 14-year-old girl is growing fast and has started her monthly periods. How does this affect her food and nutrient needs?

options.A: She only needs extra water and no other dietary changes
options.B: Her nutritional demands decrease because her body is slowing down
options.C: Her nutritional demands remain exactly the same as childhood
options.D: Her nutritional demands increase significantly to support growth and blood loss

explanation: Exactly! Rapid body growth plus monthly blood loss means she needs more energy, protein, and key minerals to stay strong and healthy.

question: Why is IEC such an important strategy in primary health care?

options.A: It replaces the need for administering routine childhood immunizations.
options.B: It helps bridge the gap between medical facts and everyday community understanding.
options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose complex tropical diseases without a doctor.
options.D: It guarantees immediate funding for rural health center construction.

explanation: Medical jargon can be confusing! IEC helps translate heavy health concepts into simple ideas that ordinary people can easily use in their daily lives.

question: What is one of the biggest physical dangers people with chronic illnesses face when they have to evacuate in a hurry?

options.A: Gaining too much weight from inactivity
options.B: Growing extra limbs
options.C: Developing temporary blindness
options.D: Losing their regular daily medications

explanation: In a sudden rush to escape, patients often leave behind their blood pressure or diabetes drugs. Nurses must check for this early!

question: What is a varicocele, which is a known physical cause of male infertility?

options.A: An infection of the prostate gland
options.B: A blockage of the vas deferens
options.C: Enlarged veins within the scrotum
options.D: The absence of a seminal vesicle

explanation: You got it! Enlarged veins in the scrotum can trap extra heat, which harms healthy sperm production. Easy peasy!

question: Why must the middle ear amplify sound vibrations before they pass into the inner ear?

options.A: Air molecules travel too fast for the cochlea to catch them
options.B: The brain cannot process low-amplitude sounds without assistance
options.C: Sound loses energy when moving from air into the fluid of the inner ear
options.D: The inner ear requires electrical current instead of physical movement

explanation: Sound waves tend to bounce off liquid surfaces. Because the inner ear is filled with fluid, the middle ear bones must boost the sound pressure so it doesn't get lost!

question: What is a common danger when researchers use very long or complex checklists during busy ward shifts?

options.A: Observer fatigue leading to rushed or guessed answers
options.B: Automatic rejection of the study by the ethics committee
options.C: Immediate breakdown of hospital computer networks
options.D: Patients refusing to take their prescribed medications

explanation: Keep it concise! When tools are too long and staff are tired, they lose focus and might just start guessing.

question: When starting a study, what does the null hypothesis (H0) usually claim?

options.A: There is a strong, proven relationship between two variables
options.B: The research study was conducted incorrectly from the start
options.C: There is no real difference or effect between groups
options.D: The new nursing intervention is guaranteed to cure all patients

explanation: Think of the null hypothesis as the 'no change' baseline. It assumes everything is normal and any small difference you see is just random chance.

question: Which Boolean operator should you use when you want to broaden your search to include synonyms?

options.A: WITH
options.B: NOT
options.C: OR
options.D: AND

explanation: The OR operator tells the database to retrieve documents containing any of the listed terms, which expands your results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which routine task helps keep a vaccine refrigerator running smoothly and prevents ice buildup?

options.A: Washing the inside walls with strong bleach daily
options.B: Placing heavy stones on top to keep doors sealed
options.C: Unplugging the unit every night before leaving
options.D: Regular defrosting and cleaning condenser coils

explanation: Routine care like defrosting keeps the compressor happy and ensures your fridge maintains the right temperature all month long.

question: An asthma patient taking steroid medications suddenly has high blood sugar readings. What should you suspect?

options.A: Severe dehydration from lack of water intake
options.B: Medication-induced alteration of glucose metabolism
options.C: A primary failure of the pancreas to produce insulin
options.D: An allergic reaction to the asthma medication

explanation: Spot on! Steroid therapy frequently messes with normal blood sugar control, even in people who have never had diabetes before.

question: What major environmental problem is caused by poorly operated, low-temperature medical incinerators?

options.A: Complete disappearance of municipal electricity grids
options.B: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the air
options.C: Immediate flooding of nearby hospital wards
options.D: Excessive production of harmless oxygen gas

explanation: Burning medical waste at low temperatures without proper filters releases nasty chemical pollutants like dioxins and furans into our air. High standards matter!

question: How can a community health nurse help support the spiritual health of a homebound patient?

options.A: By helping connect them to virtual worship services or volunteer visitors
options.B: By discouraging them from practicing any faith rituals at home
options.C: By replacing their spiritual beliefs with standard medical routines
options.D: By taking over their personal religious duties and daily prayers

explanation: Nurses act as a bridge, linking isolated patients to online services, volunteers, or groups that help keep their spiritual routines alive.

question: What is tele-nursing mainly all about?

options.A: The training of nursing students through online video lectures
options.B: A computerized machine that automatically administers medications
options.C: An online filing system used strictly for hospital record keeping
options.D: The practice of nursing care delivered over a distance using technology

explanation: You got this! Tele-nursing simply means using phones, video calls, or apps to connect with patients remotely, giving them guidance and support without needing to be right beside them.

question: Why should lab request forms never share the same pouch as a liquid specimen bottle?

options.A: To speed up the sorting process inside the central laboratory
options.B: To prevent the paperwork from being ruined if the specimen leaks
options.C: To comply with rules regarding medical record privacy
options.D: To ensure the laboratory technician reads the test name first

explanation: Great thinking! If a bottle leaks, it can soak and destroy the request form, making patient identification and testing impossible.

question: Why might a standard keyword search miss relevant articles that a MeSH search would easily find?

options.A: MeSH databases hide articles that were published before 1990
options.B: Authors use different words for the same clinical condition
options.C: Standard keywords are illegal to use in evidence-based practice
options.D: Computers cannot read lowercase letters in standard search bars

explanation: If an author uses 'heart attack' instead of 'myocardial infarction', a strict keyword search might miss it, whereas a MeSH term covers both. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which incubator type is used for growing bacteria that need extra carbon dioxide?

options.A: Standard dry-heat oven
options.B: Water distillation unit
options.C: CO2 incubator
options.D: Freezer compartment

explanation: It's all in the name! CO2 incubators are specially built to give fussy pathogens the exact gas levels they crave.

question: Which Nigerian food item is an excellent local source of both plant protein and healthy fats?

options.A: Melon seeds (egusi)
options.B: Refined white sugar
options.C: Packaged soft drinks
options.D: Polished white garri

explanation: Spot on! Egusi is packed with valuable plant proteins and healthy fats, making it a powerhouse for local nutrition.

question: How is general hospital waste different from infectious waste?

options.A: Infectious waste is always heavier than general waste boxes
options.B: General waste requires special incineration before leaving the ward
options.C: General waste is non-hazardous and similar to normal household trash
options.D: Infectious waste comes only from the hospital kitchen

explanation: Exactly! General waste has no contamination risk (like empty paper packaging), unlike infectious items that carry pathogens.

question: How do everyday stressors affect the development of neurasthenia?

options.A: They permanently alter brain chemistry instantly
options.B: They prevent any form of physical illness from occurring
options.C: They deplete coping reserves over time and trigger exhaustion
options.D: They have no impact on mental or physical health

explanation: You nailed it! Constant daily pressure slowly drains a person's nervous energy until they feel totally burnt out. Keep going!

question: Which visual chart is most commonly used to map out a project timeline in a research proposal?

options.A: Scatter plot
options.B: Flowchart diagram
options.C: Gantt chart
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: A Gantt chart is a handy bar chart layout that helps you schedule out your project tasks and deadlines across the weeks or months of your study.

question: What does 'novelty' mean when picking a research topic?

options.A: The topic has already been researched a thousand times
options.B: The research project is written in the form of a novel
options.C: The study adds new knowledge or a fresh perspective to the field
options.D: The study uses brand new computers purchased from abroad

explanation: Novelty simply means bringing a fresh idea or a new angle to nursing so our profession keeps moving forward!

question: Why do you need to check a patient's medication list before they get an EMG test?

options.A: To ensure the patient has taken their daily antibiotics
options.B: To prevent allergic reactions to the conductive gel used
options.C: To stop pain medications that would numb the skin entirely
options.D: To check for drugs that thin the blood and risk bleeding

explanation: Because an EMG involves placing thin needles directly into muscle tissue, taking blood thinners can put the patient at risk for internal bleeding or hematomas.

question: A patient tagged as yellow suddenly starts gasping for air and showing signs of shock. What should you do?

options.A: Ask the patient to walk over to the green area
options.B: Leave the patient in the yellow category because triage tags never change
options.C: Re-tag the patient as red and provide immediate life-saving care
options.D: Move the patient to the black category immediately

explanation: Triage isn't a one-time thing; patient conditions change fast! If someone gets worse, you upgrade their tag right away to get them urgent help.

question: What is a major risk of depending too much on donor funding for national healthcare?

options.A: Private hospitals will take over all government teaching hospitals
options.B: Local healthcare workers will refuse to treat insured patients
options.C: Patients will stop paying out-of-pocket for their medications
options.D: Services may collapse when donor priorities change or funding ends

explanation: Well reasoned! External aid can be unstable. If foreign partners pack up or shift their focus, programs without local backup can easily crash.

question: What is the main goal of giving oxygen therapy with a face mask?

options.A: Permanently cure chronic respiratory diseases
options.B: Lower the patient's baseline body temperature
options.C: Maintain safe arterial oxygen saturation levels
options.D: Increase the patient's total body weight

explanation: You give extra oxygen mainly to keep the patient's blood oxygen in a safe range and stop their tissues from lacking air. You've got this!

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops diseases from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination and health promotion. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is your very first nursing action if an abdominal wound suddenly pops open and organs are exposed?

options.A: Cover the organs with sterile saline-soaked dressings and call the surgeon.
options.B: Use your gloved fingers to push the organs back inside.
options.C: Wrap a tight binder around the belly to squeeze the organs back in.
options.D: Leave the wound completely open to the fresh air.

explanation: Keep those exposed organs moist with sterile saline gauze so they don't dry out while you call for emergency surgical help. Emergency handled like a champ!

question: A busy ward has only one working patient lift, and both the day and night shifts keep arguing over who gets to use it. What is driving this conflict?

options.A: Personality clashes
options.B: Role ambiguity
options.C: Resource scarcity
options.D: Value differences

explanation: When important tools or equipment are in short supply, tension builds up fast. That is classic resource scarcity in action!

question: A nurse organizes a community screening program to check blood sugar levels in adults over forty. Which level of prevention does this represent?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Screenings are designed to find hidden health problems early so treatment can start right away, which is secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h2)

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a nurse on a hospital ward?

options.A: Being immune from any form of peer review or performance evaluation
options.B: Working night shifts without physical security guards on the ward
options.C: Never experiencing stress or fatigue during clinical duties
options.D: Feeling safe to report errors and speak up without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: You got it! Psychological safety means trust—knowing you can speak up honestly to protect your patients.

question: An unresponsive patient is brought in. After you make sure their airway and breathing are okay, what is your next immediate step?

options.A: Inquiring about dietary preferences for hospital meals
options.B: Checking circulation, pulse rate, and blood pressure
options.C: Reviewing the patient's employment history and workplace
options.D: Measuring the exact height and weight on a scale

explanation: Following the ABCDE routine, 'C' comes right after Airway and Breathing so you can check for blood flow and signs of shock.

question: Which part of an antibody molecule binds directly to a specific antigen?

options.A: Y-shaped stem
options.B: Complement tail
options.C: Constant region
options.D: Variable region

explanation: The tips of the Y-shaped antibody have a variable region that fits onto antigens like a lock and key.

question: If household incomes in a community suddenly increase, what change in healthcare use are we likely to see?

options.A: An increase in the uptake of elective and preventive health services
options.B: A total cessation of visits to traditional local healers
options.C: No alteration in how residents access local health clinics
options.D: A sharp decrease in the number of emergency room admissions

explanation: Spot on! When people have more money in their pockets, they can finally afford wellness checks, vitamins, and elective care before emergencies happen.

question: Why do we want an infant calm and sitting upright when checking their fontanelles?

options.A: Sitting upright makes the posterior fontanelle larger and easier to see
options.B: A calm baby will allow the nurse to measure skull circumference accurately
options.C: Crying or lying flat can temporarily cause false bulging
options.D: Crying causes the fontanelle to sink and look dehydrated

explanation: You nailed it. Straining or crying pushes pressure upward, making a normal soft spot look like it's bulging when it's actually fine.

question: Which of these is NOT a daily job for a nurse in infection control?

options.A: Manufacturing the chemical disinfectants used in the hospital
options.B: Watching out for accidental breaks in sterile technique
options.C: Teaching patients how to wash their hands properly
options.D: Throwing away used needles safely in puncture-proof boxes

explanation: You got it! Factories make the chemical solutions; nurses are right at the bedside using them and keeping our patients safe.

question: What is the main purpose of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To legally sign medical documents on behalf of busy attending physicians
options.B: To order hospital kitchen meals based on patient dietary preferences
options.C: To schedule nursing shift rotations and manage monthly hospital payrolls
options.D: To provide automated prompts and guidelines that assist clinicians in making safe choices

explanation: You got it! CDSS software acts like a smart assistant, analyzing patient data to give helpful alerts and evidence-based tips.

question: In safety management, what is considered the MOST effective way to deal with a hazard?

options.A: Using administrative policies
options.B: Conducting safety training
options.C: Elimination of the hazard
options.D: Wearing protective gloves

explanation: If you completely remove the danger, nobody can get hurt by it! That makes elimination the ultimate win in safety.

question: What are the small bumps on the surface of the tongue that house taste buds called?

options.A: Alveoli
options.B: Fauces
options.C: Uvula
options.D: Papillae

explanation: Papillae are the visible projections on the tongue surface that contain sensory receptors for taste. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h3)

question: Where should a nurse NOT use a local anesthetic mixed with adrenaline?

options.A: On a clean scalp wound
options.B: On a forearm abrasion
options.C: On a large thigh laceration
options.D: On the fingers or toes

explanation: Adrenaline causes blood vessels to constrict tightly, which can cut off blood supply entirely in digits and lead to tissue death. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: How should a nurse respond when a caregiver expresses fear and doubt about a routine vaccine?

options.A: Ignore the question and administer the injection without speaking
options.B: Listen with empathy, validate concerns, and provide clear factual information
options.C: Scold the caregiver for putting their child's life at immediate risk
options.D: Tell the caregiver that rumors are illegal and punishable by law

explanation: You've got this! Building trust through patience and gentle, honest education is always the best way to help caregivers feel confident.

question: Why must a nurse leader look at all four parts of Deming's framework together?

options.A: Because licensing boards force you to recite all four terms in patient charts
options.B: Because treating them separately will crash the hospital computers
options.C: Because the four components overlap and deeply influence one another in real practice
options.D: Because focusing on just one part is illegal in healthcare

explanation: They work best as a team! Understanding people (psychology), systems, variation, and theory all blend together when solving daily ward challenges.

question: What is the heart of constructivist learning theory?

options.A: Behavior changes only occur through strict reward systems
options.B: Knowledge is an exact copy of what the textbook states
options.C: Learners actively build new knowledge using past experiences
options.D: Students learn best when they sit quietly and listen to lectures

explanation: You aren't just an empty bucket waiting to be filled! Constructivism means you connect new nursing concepts to what you already know from your own life and experiences.

question: A nurse wants to know how many clinic visitors have a weight above a certain mark. Which graph should she check?

options.A: A 'greater than' ogive
options.B: A 'less than' ogive
options.C: A simple pie chart
options.D: A standard bar graph

explanation: You're doing great! A 'greater than' ogive is specifically built to track totals that exceed or lie above specific cut-off points.

question: What was a major headache with early psychiatric classification systems?

options.A: Governments refused to fund any mental health research
options.B: They focused exclusively on genetic markers
options.C: Too many laboratory tests were required for admission
options.D: Inconsistencies between hospitals caused clinical confusion

explanation: Back in the day, different hospitals used totally different terms. This made sharing notes or comparing treatments a real struggle!

question: During which stage of sleep do you experience vivid dreams and temporary muscle relaxation?

options.A: Stage 3 NREM sleep
options.B: Stage 1 NREM sleep
options.C: Stage 2 NREM sleep
options.D: REM sleep

explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is when most dreaming happens. Your body temporarily relaxes your muscles so you don't act out your dreams!

question: What is the main focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) right after a disaster?

options.A: Conducting deep psychoanalysis and clinical psychotherapy
options.B: Forcing survivors to recount every detail of the traumatic event
options.C: Providing humane comfort, safety, and practical support
options.D: Prescribing long-term psychiatric medications to all victims

explanation: Great job! PFA is all about calming immediate distress and giving practical help, not forcing deep therapy or heavy counseling right away.

question: Which cranial nerve is mainly responsible for controlling the muscles of the oesophagus?

options.A: Glossopharyngeal nerve
options.B: Hypoglossal nerve
options.C: Trigeminal nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: Correct! The vagus nerve is the major highway for signals that coordinate those smooth swallowing contractions.

question: A patient with diabetes looks shaky, dizzy, and is sweating before lunch. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Administer the scheduled dose of daily long-acting insulin
options.B: Send a blood sample to the laboratory for an HbA1c test
options.C: Encourage the patient to sleep until the symptoms pass
options.D: Check blood glucose levels and prepare a fast-acting carbohydrate

explanation: Shakiness and sweating are red flags for low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Always check the blood glucose first and have a fast sugar source ready! Patient safety comes first.

question: A patient with severe malaria arrives late at a clinic because they couldn't afford transport or consultation fees. What economic factor is mainly to blame?

options.A: Excessive government spending on preventative health education
options.B: Too many nurses working in rural primary health centers
options.C: High reliance on out-of-pocket health expenditure
options.D: An oversupply of subsidized pharmaceutical drugs in local markets

explanation: When patients have to pay cash out of pocket right away, it creates a financial barrier that delays life-saving care.

question: A hospital wants shock-resistant drives for mobile nursing carts that load patient charts instantly. Which one should they pick?

options.A: Compact Disc (CD-ROM)
options.B: Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
options.C: Magnetic tape reel
options.D: Solid State Drive (SSD)

explanation: SSDs have no spinning parts, making them super tough for mobile carts rolling down hospital corridors and much faster than old-school hard drives!

question: What is a major benefit of buying local Nigerian food staples during harvest season?

options.A: They are always imported from abroad
options.B: They have longer artificial shelf lives
options.C: They require no washing or cooking
options.D: They are cheaper and more nutritious

explanation: In-season local foods are harvested at peak ripeness, offering better nutrients at lower market prices due to high supply. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a medical evacuation (medevac)?

options.A: To move a patient to a facility with higher-level care
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital treatment
options.C: To clear crowded hospital beds for new admissions
options.D: To provide permanent long-term rehabilitation therapy

explanation: Medevac is all about bridging the gap! It safely transports patients from places with limited resources to specialized centers where they can get the exact treatment they need.

question: Which group of patients is excused from fasting in almost all major religions?

options.A: The sick, pregnant women, and the elderly
options.B: Individuals traveling outside their home country
options.C: Only children under the age of five years
options.D: Athletes and people engaged in heavy manual labor

explanation: Major religions always put health and safety first, offering clear exemptions from fasting for vulnerable groups like the sick, pregnant women, and the elderly.

question: A new nurse is sorting waste on a busy ward. Which action shows they are following safety rules correctly?

options.A: Dropping a used syringe directly into a puncture-resistant box without recapping
options.B: Tossing blood-stained gauze into the ordinary office waste bin
options.C: Recapping a needle carefully using both hands before disposal
options.D: Storing expired medications in the ward refrigerator next to patient snacks

explanation: Brilliant! Dropping the used syringe straight into the safety box without trying to recap it is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries.

question: In the TSSU, what does the inventory rule 'FIFO' stand for?

options.A: Filtered-Instrument, Filtered-Object
options.B: Final-Item, Final-Order
options.C: Fast-Inspection, Fast-Operation
options.D: First-In, First-Out

explanation: Correct! FIFO means the supplies that arrived first get used first, keeping items from sitting on shelves past their expiration dates.

question: What movement decreases the angle between two bones, like bending your elbow?

options.A: Extension
options.B: Flexion
options.C: Abduction
options.D: Pronation

explanation: You nailed it! Flexion is bending a limb to decrease the angle at a joint—like bringing your hand closer to your shoulder.

question: Why do cooks love adding waterleaf to traditional Nigerian soups and stews?

options.A: It turns the broth into a solid gel when allowed to cool down
options.B: It serves as a strong preservative to keep soups from spoiling quickly
options.C: It acts as a natural thickening agent while adding moisture and vitamins
options.D: It completely replaces the need for adding palm oil to the pot

explanation: Spot on! Waterleaf breaks down nicely during cooking to give soups a rich texture while boosting the vitamin content.

question: What is the main risk of poor water management in heavily irrigated dry lands over time?

options.A: Complete freezing of the earth
options.B: Excessive forest growth
options.C: Soil salinization
options.D: Volcanic eruptions

explanation: When irrigation water evaporates too quickly in hot places, it leaves behind salt deposits that eventually ruin the soil for farming.

question: What is the primary purpose of health care financing in a national health system?

options.A: Raising, pooling, and allocating funds for health services
options.B: Purchasing pharmaceutical manufacturing plants
options.C: Recruiting international medical volunteers
options.D: Setting international medical licensing examinations

explanation: Health financing is specifically concerned with how money is collected, combined, and spent to provide health care to the population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h1)

question: A ward normally discharges 5 patients a morning, but today 12 left at once because a visiting consultant cleared them all. What kind of variation is this?

options.A: Common cause variation
options.B: Random statistical noise
options.C: Normal baseline fluctuation
options.D: Special cause variation

explanation: You nailed it! That sudden surge went beyond the normal daily routine because of one clear event—a visiting consultant clearing the beds.

question: What is the name of the popular screening tool used specifically to check nutritional risk in older adults?

options.A: Braden Skin Risk Scale
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Mini Nutritional Assessment
options.D: Morse Fall Scale

explanation: That's the Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA)! It's a quick, handy tool nurses use to catch nutrition risks early in older patients.

question: When should the nurse stop the repeating cycles of fluid instillation and drainage during a gastric lavage?

options.A: When the collection bucket is half filled with fluid
options.B: When exactly one hour has passed on the clock
options.C: When the returned lavage fluid runs completely clear
options.D: When the patient asks for a glass of cold water

explanation: The wash cycles continue until the fluid coming back out is completely clear of toxins, pills, or debris, indicating the stomach is empty. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h5)

question: What was a major focus of Nigeria's original 1988 National Population Policy?

options.A: Banning traditional birth attendants nationwide
options.B: Mandatory relocation of rural populations to cities
options.C: Providing free university education for all citizens
options.D: Setting a limit on the number of children per woman

explanation: Back in 1988, the policy tried to slow down rapid population growth by suggesting a specific target for how many children a woman should have. It faced a lot of cultural pushback, but that was the main strategy at the time!

question: How does having a clear hypothesis help a nurse researcher?

options.A: It guarantees that funding will be instantly approved by the government
options.B: It provides a clear prediction of expected relationships to guide testing
options.C: It stops patients from withdrawing their consent midway through
options.D: It eliminates the need for any statistical calculations at the end

explanation: Spot on! A hypothesis gives your study a roadmap so you know exactly what relationship you are testing.

question: How does a hemorrhagic stroke cause damage to the brain?

options.A: By causing bleeding that increases pressure and compresses brain cells
options.B: By causing a permanent lack of glucose without altering pressure
options.C: By replacing normal neurons with fibrous scar tissue over time
options.D: By triggering widespread bacterial growth in the ventricles

explanation: Spot on! When a blood vessel bursts inside the skull, the pooling blood builds up pressure and squeezes the surrounding delicate brain tissue.

question: How would you simply describe an autoimmune disease?

options.A: A condition where the immune system attacks the body's own healthy tissues
options.B: A temporary infection spread through close contact in a community
options.C: An immediate allergic reaction caused by exposure to environmental pollen
options.D: A genetic deficiency that prevents the production of red blood cells

explanation: In autoimmune diseases, the immune system gets confused and mistakenly treats friendly, healthy body cells as enemies, attacking them by mistake.

question: Why is it useful for nurse managers to understand basic cost elements?

options.A: To diagnose complex patient illnesses faster
options.B: To calculate individual doctor salaries
options.C: To track spending and justify unit budgets
options.D: To negotiate lower pharmaceutical taxes

explanation: When nurse leaders know where money goes, they can manage their wards better and defend why their unit needs certain resources. Great leadership skill to pick up early!

question: Why is good communication especially critical in busy primary health clinics?

options.A: It prevents dangerous mistakes caused by misunderstood instructions
options.B: It removes the need for doctors in the clinic
options.C: It allows the nurse to spend less time working with patients
options.D: It completely stops patients from seeking traditional healers

explanation: When clinics are crowded and resources are stretched, clear communication ensures patients still understand their medications and care instructions, avoiding serious errors. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h1)

question: How does keeping your muscles tense for too long due to poor posture affect your body?

options.A: It builds permanent muscle mass faster than regular exercise
options.B: It increases the oxygen supply to the overworked muscle fibers
options.C: It cools down the body temperature in surrounding joints
options.D: It reduces adequate blood flow, leading to fatigue and pain

explanation: Spot on! Constant muscle tension squeezes your blood vessels, starving your muscles of oxygen and leaving you feeling sore and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: How can poverty make health education harder to put into practice?

options.A: It automatically cures all infectious diseases
options.B: Patients may struggle to afford recommended foods or medications
options.C: It prevents community members from gathering together
options.D: It stops nurses from speaking local languages

explanation: Financial hardship makes it tough for patients to follow health advice that requires buying prescribed drugs or specific nutritious foods.

question: Why do nurses commonly use 70-90% alcohol to wipe down small items like medication vials?

options.A: They leave a long-lasting protective film that repels dust for weeks
options.B: They evaporate quickly and effectively denature microbial proteins
options.C: They destroy all bacterial endospores within two minutes of contact
options.D: They are completely safe to ingest if they accidentally mix with IV fluids

explanation: Alcohol is a ward favorite because it acts fast against germs and dries up quickly without leaving any sticky residue behind.

question: How can you help patients without smartphones benefit from tele-nursing?

options.A: By forcing them to purchase expensive tablets immediately
options.B: By using basic voice calls and SMS text reminders
options.C: By refusing to provide any health education to them
options.D: By stopping all forms of remote follow-up care

explanation: Exactly! Simple voice calls and text messages bridge the gap so patients without smart devices still get quality care.

question: How does severe malnutrition with low blood protein (albumin) affect highly protein-bound drugs?

options.A: Kidneys flush the medication out immediately without any effect
options.B: The liver instantly destroys the drug before it reaches any target
options.C: More free drug is available in the blood, increasing toxicity risk
options.D: The drug binds tighter to tissues and never enters the bloodstream

explanation: Think of blood proteins like seats on a bus for drugs. If there aren't enough seats (albumin), more drugs float around freely in the blood, which can easily lead to an accidental overdose effect! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h3)

question: Which medication do doctors commonly start early in pregnancy to help prevent pre-eclampsia in women with sickle cell disease?

options.A: High-dose hydroxyurea
options.B: Low-dose aspirin
options.C: Therapeutic penicillin
options.D: Intravenous iron sucrose

explanation: Brilliant! Low-dose aspirin is a helpful tool started early on to protect the placenta and lower the risk of pre-eclampsia.

question: A patient stays home from work, complains of body aches to their partner, and rests in bed. Which stage of illness behavior is this?

options.A: Dependent client role
options.B: Assuming the sick role
options.C: Recovery stage
options.D: Medical care contact stage

explanation: Spot on! At this stage, the person accepts that they are sick, gets support from loved ones, and takes a break from their normal daily duties.
